conflicts.description: The Concord of Light wants to spend scarce power shielding the grid, while the Seedkeepers argue that only the vault's seeds can rebuild fields scorched by the beam, forcing the heroes to cross the Wastes without official support.
conflicts.name: Seeds Versus Stability

conflicts.description: The Tidewrights hold the only safe routes through the Saltglass Wastes, but resent the arcologies that once closed their gates to them, and demand a reckoning before they will help.
conflicts.name: The Price of a Guide

description: In a near-future Earth ravaged by climate collapse, humanity survives inside a network of solar-powered arcologies called Greenholds. Each is a living city of terraced gardens, mirrored light-wells and shimmering photovoltaic canopies, tended by communities who treat every watt and every seed as sacred. Beyond their walls lie the toxic Wastes: salt flats, acid marshes and dust seas where old-world ruins slowly decay. The tone is hopeful. Cooperation, ingenuity and care for living things are slowly mending a broken planet. A rogue weather satellite, a relic of the old climate-control age, has begun focusing sunlight on the western Greenhold and a massive solar storm is approaching. The only hope lies in a forgotten seed vault across the Wastes, and in a young engineer and a reclusive botanist willing to cross them to reach it. The world is built on solar power, biology, craft and trust, with tools such as sun-lenses, bioluminescent beacons, sail-skiffs and mechanical ingenuity in place of explosives or heavy weapons.

factions.description: The governing council of the Greenholds, devoted to preserving the solar grid and the arcology network at nearly any cost.
factions.name: The Concord of Light

factions.description: A scattered order of botanists who preserve biodiversity and believe the old vault must be reopened, even against the Concord's caution.
factions.name: The Seedkeepers

factions.description: Salvagers and sail-skiff pilots of the ruins, who guide travelers across the Wastes for fair trade and who distrust the arcologies' isolation.
factions.name: The Tidewrights

history.description: Climate collapse destroyed old-world nations, boiled the oceans' edges and turned farmland to salt desert.
history.name: The Great Scorch

history.description: Survivors raised the first solar arcology and wrote the Seed Oath.
history.name: Founding of Heliopolis Core

history.description: Seedkeepers sealed Emberroot Vault after a succession dispute and its location slipped from official records.
history.name: The Vault Sealing

history.description: An aging weather satellite broke from its orbit control and began to track solar arrays, scorching Westerly's outer canopy.
history.name: The Satellite Drifts

locations.description: The westernmost solar arcology, a terraced city of glass and living wood whose photovoltaic canopies are now threatened by the rogue satellite's focused beam.
locations.name: Westerly Greenhold

locations.description: The central Greenhold and seat of the Concord of Light, where the Solar Assembly debates how to ration energy and resources during the crisis.
locations.name: Heliopolis Core

locations.description: A vast toxic plain of fused salt and glittering glass, where mirage storms and acid pools hide the safe paths that travelers must learn to read.
locations.name: The Saltglass Wastes

locations.description: A drowned old-world port city whose rusting cranes shelter the Tidewrights, scavengers who repair sail-skiffs powered by solar cells.
locations.name: Rustwake Ruins

locations.description: A forgotten vault carved beneath a dormant ridge, powered by a failing solar array and holding the seeds of thousands of lost species.
locations.name: Emberroot Seed Vault

name: The Greenhold Reach

rules.statement: All Greenhold infrastructure runs on solar power; stored light in crystal-lattice cells is the currency of survival and is strictly rationed.
Explosive chemistry is abandoned and taboo; tools and defenses rely on lenses, mechanics, tension and living materials.
Exposure to Wastes air and water without filter-masks and sealed skins causes sickness within hours; shelter is needed at night when mirage storms rise.
Solar storms disable unshielded electronics and surge through grid cables, so travelers must carry shielded cases or work by hand.
Every Greenhold citizen swears the Seed Oath: no living species may be knowingly let to perish if it can be saved.
The rogue satellite refocuses its beam on a predictable cycle of roughly one sweep per day, tracking the brightest solar installation.
